discovery: Photonic crystals and the photonic band gap
motivation: In 1987 Yablonovitch and John independently proposed that a periodic dielectric structure can open a complete photonic band gap. Yablonovitch showed it could suppress spontaneous emission, and John showed it could cause strong localization of light. Yablonovitch then built the first three-dimensional band-gap crystal. Joannopoulos turned these ideas into a predictive, quantitative science. He brought the band-structure methods of solid-state physics to electromagnetism, designed defect cavities, waveguides and complete-gap structures, and set out the principles the field still uses. Together they made light controllable the way electrons are in semiconductors. The concept now underpins photonic-crystal fibres, high-Q nanocavities for cavity QED, low-threshold lasers, slow light, integrated silicon photonics, and topological photonics with bound states in the continuum. It has transformed both fundamental optics and technology.
